problem: The answer says mobility degradation would "make gm fall as overdrive grows". That is wrong. With µeff = µ0/(1 + θVov) and ID = ½kn′(W/L)Vov²/(1 + θVov), the transconductance is gm = kn′(W/L)·Vov(2 + θVov)/(1 + θVov)², which rises monotonically with overdrive and only levels off toward kn′/θ. It never decreases, so a student who checks the algebra will be confused, and the stated contrast with velocity saturation is false.
fix: Replace the last sentence with: "Mobility degradation alone keeps the current close to quadratic in form and only flattens gm toward the constant kn′/θ; it does not make the current itself linear in overdrive the way velocity saturation does."

problem: "a process constant of a few tenths of a volt inverse for thin oxides" is awkward and the symbol is not given in unit form, unlike every other quantity in the chapter.
fix: Write: "θ is the mobility degradation coefficient in 1/V, a process constant typically between 0.1 V⁻¹ and 1 V⁻¹ for thin oxides."

problem: "a mixed set gives an answer off by 10⁴" is vague and not right for every quantity: cm²/V·s to m²/V·s is a factor 10⁻⁴, but fF/µm² to F/m² is only 10⁻³, so a student cannot tell which factor applies where.
fix: Give the conversions explicitly: "µ in cm²/V·s becomes m²/V·s by multiplying by 10⁻⁴; Cox in fF/µm² becomes F/m² by multiplying by 10⁻³; vsat in cm/s becomes m/s by multiplying by 10⁻². Convert everything to one set before substituting."
